name: jusText (Jan Pomikalek, Masaryk University Brno; reference Python implementation miso-belica/justext, plus a C++ port and a Java reimplementation inside dkpro-c4corpus). Introduced in the PhD thesis 'Removing Boilerplate and Duplicate Content from Web Corpora' (2011). AND newspaper3k (codelucas/newspaper, PyPI `newspaper3k`), with its live fork newspaper4k (AndyTheFactory). Related lineage: newspaper is Goose-derived, so goose3 and news-please are cousins.
kind: Two libraries with different scopes, deliberately paired here because they represent opposite failure archetypes. jusText is a pure boilerplate-removal FUNCTION with no I/O. newspaper3k/4k is an end-to-end PIPELINE -- fetcher, crawler, feed parser, extractor, image downloader and NLP summariser in one object -- which makes it the only item in this batch that is a network client as well as an extractor.
maturity: jusText: mature, frozen, and quietly load-bearing. It is not fashionable but it has been used to build multi-language web corpora at 20 TB of input HTML producing 70-billion-token corpora (the Sketch Engine / TenTen line), which is production evidence at a scale most items here cannot claim. newspaper3k: ABANDONED -- no update since September 2020, and it is still the version most tutorials and downstream code pin, which makes it a live supply-chain and correctness hazard. newspaper4k: healthy, actively released, API-compatible fork, and the only version that should be considered.
license: jusText: BSD-3-Clause. newspaper3k: MIT. newspaper4k: dual MIT / Apache-2.0. All three permit use here without restriction. jusText additionally requires per-language STOPLISTS, which ship with it and inherit its license; that dependency is an algorithmic constraint, not a licensing one, but it is worth noting that adopting the algorithm means adopting a data file per language.
keeps_and_discards: jusText is the most precisely specified algorithm in this batch and the specification is short enough to state exactly. Preprocessing: strip
structure_preserved: jusText: block sequence with class labels and nothing else -- no nesting, no list structure, no table relations, no typed headings beyond the fact that heading blocks were specially handled during classification. It is a labelled flat sequence, structurally comparable to Boilerpipe. Its one structural virtue is the explicit heading promotion, which means headings tend to SURVIVE next to the content they head rather than being discarded as short low-density blocks -- a small, deliberate preservation of document hierarchy that Boilerpipe lacks. newspaper3k returns a plain text string for the article body, so structure is entirely gone; what it preserves instead is a METADATA RECORD (title, authors, date, images), which is a different axis and the reason people use it. Neither models shadow boundaries in any way; both consume serialized HTML through lxml, open shadow roots are absent, closed roots unrepresentable, no unreachable marker emitted.
interactive_elements: jusText discards them, and does so through one explicit rule plus one statistical consequence: <select> contents are marked boilerplate by name, and everything else interactive falls out because controls are short and link-dense, failing LENGTH_LOW and MAX_LINK_DENSITY. Anchors are not preserved as links -- only their contribution to link density is used, then the text is emitted or dropped. newspaper3k likewise discards all controls; its output is a text blob plus metadata, with no element types at all. Neither has a toggle to retain affordances. jusText's <select> rule is worth flagging as the only place in this batch where a control type is named explicitly in an algorithm's preprocessing, and it is named in order to delete it.
interactive_state_fidelity: Zero for both, with no partial credit and no toggle. disabled, checked, selected, aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-pressed, aria-current and role are neither read as features nor representable in output. jusText's <select> handling is the exact inverse of state preservation: the one place a stateful control appears in the specification, it appears as a thing to discard. The token cost of state is zero and the affordance count is zero for both. What makes the pair instructive is newspaper3k's METADATA record: it demonstrates that this family is perfectly willing to carry a structured side-channel of extracted attributes (authors, date, images) alongside the text -- so the absence of an interactive-state side-channel is a choice about what is considered valuable, not a limitation of the representation. A 'tag plus interactivity' record is the same shape as newspaper's metadata record, pointed at a different target.
layout_awareness: jusText: none geometric, and less than most -- it has no visibility pass at all beyond dropping <script>/<style>/<header>, so it does not even read inline display:none. Its length and density thresholds are typographic proxies in the Boilerpipe spirit rather than geometric reads. newspaper3k: none geometric in the extractor, BUT it reaches for a geometric-adjacent signal by network: its top-image selection needs image DIMENSIONS to decide which image is most prominent, and since the HTML often does not declare them, the library DOWNLOADS candidate images to measure them. That is layout information obtained by fetching, which is a category no other item in this batch occupies and which has direct privacy consequences (see leaks_outward). [uncertain] on exactly which code paths in newspaper4k still fetch images versus reading declared attributes first.
javascript_required: Neither runs scripts. jusText is a pure function over parsed HTML; newspaper3k fetches raw HTML with an HTTP client and parses it with lxml. Both return the shell for client-rendered pages, silently. For newspaper3k the no-JS property is NOT a privacy benefit, because it compensates by making many separate HTTP requests of its own (the article, the images, the feeds, the category pages) -- it trades script execution for crawler traffic, which is the more detectable of the two. For jusText the property is genuinely inert: no scripts, no requests, nothing observable. In this project's architecture the browser has already executed the page, so jusText's algorithm is directly applicable to already-composed text and newspaper3k's fetching layer is not merely unnecessary but actively harmful.
evaluation_method: jusText was evaluated against CLEANEVAL, the shared-task methodology of its era, where systems are scored on text overlap with human-cleaned reference documents; Pomikalek reports it outperforming or keeping pace with the CleanEval field. The thesis frames the work as corpus construction, so the operative validation is EXTRINSIC and large: the algorithm was used to build multi-language corpora from 20 TB of HTML into 70 billion tokens, and the argument is that the resulting corpora are linguistically usable. That is a downstream-utility oracle in the same family as BLOGS06 and DCLM, though stated less rigorously. Modern re-measurement comes from Trafilatura's segment-level benchmark. newspaper4k reports F1 0.9460 on the ScrapingHub/Scraperhub benchmark and F1 0.9015 on the NAEB dataset, both article-only corpora scored against reference article text, and both self-reported by the fork maintainer as improvements over newspaper3k 0.2.8.
corpus_size_and_origins: jusText's primary evaluation corpus is CleanEval -- 684 English plus 653 Chinese pages downloaded in 2006, published 2007 -- which is the oldest and narrowest corpus quoted anywhere in this batch, and its extrinsic evidence is the TenTen corpus line, which is genuinely web-scale (20 TB input) but has no ground truth at all: enormous corpus, zero annotation, exactly the DCLM shape. newspaper's numbers rest on the ScrapingHub article-extraction-benchmark (181 English news article pages, published 2019, never refreshed) and the NAEB dataset, whose size, origin count and collection date I could not verify -- [uncertain]. Every corpus behind both tools is article-or-news-dominated. No corpus behind either contains a live page, a rendered SPA, a consent-gated capture or a shadow-DOM component. Note in particular that jusText's headline reputation rests on a 2006 corpus while its production credibility rests on an unannotated 20 TB pile; there is nothing in between, and nothing recent.
reported_precision_recall: jusText, in Trafilatura's segment-level benchmark (990 documents, 2,951 text and 2,966 boilerplate segments, run 2026-08-04): justext 3.0.2 with a CUSTOM configuration scores P 0.864 / R 0.859 / accuracy 0.862 / F 0.862, placing third behind trafilatura 2.2.0 at 0.924 and magic-html at 0.889, and ahead of news-please 0.836, readability-lxml 0.826 and goose3 0.810. The word 'custom' in that row matters and is easy to miss: the figure is for tuned thresholds, not defaults, which means the published number is not what a caller gets out of the box. newspaper4k 0.9.6 self-reports F1 0.9460 on ScrapingHub and F1 0.9015 on NAEB. Note the incomparability: 0.862 (segment classification, mixed corpus, competitor-run) and 0.9460 (article text overlap, 181 news pages, self-run) are not on the same scale and must never be placed in the same ranking, which is exactly what casual comparisons of these tools do. jusText does not appear in WCXB's published leaderboard rows I could retrieve, so its standing on a modern multi-archetype corpus is [uncertain] and probably poor for the reasons under page_archetype_coverage.
independent_oracle: jusText has the better claim, and it is the linguistic one: STOP-WORD DENSITY is grounded in a testable property of natural language (function words occur at a stable rate in grammatical prose) rather than in a premise about page structure. That means the feature can be validated against a linguistic corpus with no web pages involved at all -- an oracle genuinely independent of the extraction task, and the only such grounding in this batch. Whether the THRESHOLDS (0.30/0.32) are right remains a fitted question, but the FEATURE is falsifiable outside the domain. The CleanEval oracle is the usual human-cleaned reference sharing the main-content premise, and the corpus-construction evidence is downstream-utility with no reference. newspaper has no independent oracle: article-text overlap on news pages, self-reported, against a premise the tool encodes.
evidence_independence: jusText's CleanEval claim is AUTHOR-RUN (Pomikalek reporting his own system's shared-task standing), and its 0.862 figure is COMPETITOR-RUN by Trafilatura's author -- who ranks his own tool first at 0.924 and jusText third. That competitor-run placement is nonetheless the more credible of the two, since a competitor has no incentive to flatter jusText, and third place in a rival's benchmark is a stronger signal than first place in one's own. newspaper4k's 0.9460 and 0.9015 are entirely SELF-REPORTED by the fork maintainer, on benchmarks selected by the maintainer, framed as improvements over the version he forked -- the least independent evidence in this batch, and it should not be cited alongside third-party numbers without that label. Neither tool has been measured by anyone with no stake. The general pattern across this whole batch now holds without exception: every headline extraction figure in circulation is produced either by the tool's author or by a direct competitor, and the only defensible use of any of them is to compare a tool against itself across corpora.
page_archetype_coverage: Both are article-shaped, and jusText's failure on other archetypes is not merely empirical but ANALYTIC -- it can be read directly off the thresholds. A block must exceed 70 characters and carry over 30% function words to be good, and must sit under 0.2 link density. A search-results listing fails all three simultaneously (short entries, low function-word density, near-total link density). A product page is attribute-value fragments: short, function-word-poor, rejected. A forum is many sub-70-character posts resolved by context, and if the surrounding context is navigation the whole thread resolves to bad. A documentation page is code and tables carrying almost no function words and is rejected as ungrammatical, which for jusText is not a bug -- the algorithm's stated goal is to keep 'mainly text containing full sentences' for LINGUISTIC corpora, so non-sentence content is out of scope by design. newspaper is explicitly news-only and does not pretend otherwise; on a non-article page it returns a plausible-looking but arbitrary text blob plus metadata, which is worse than refusing. For this project's target population -- listings, results pages, forums, product pages, documentation -- jusText is a near-total rejection and newspaper is a confident wrong answer.
script_and_locale_behaviour: This is the axis on which the pair most sharply diverges, and jusText is the batch's clearest case of a tool that is EXPLICITLY language-parameterised rather than accidentally language-biased. jusText requires a STOPLIST per language and cannot run at all without one: the central feature is undefined absent a function-word list, so adding a language is a data-authoring task, and the algorithm's behaviour on an unlisted language is not degradation but failure. That honesty is a virtue -- the language dependence is in the interface rather than buried in a threshold -- but the consequence is severe for CJK and other whitespace-free scripts, where 'fraction of words that are function words' presupposes a word segmentation the algorithm does not perform, and where the character-count thresholds (70/200) mean something entirely different per unit of information. CleanEval's Chinese half is the only cross-script evidence and it is 2006-era. No RTL handling and no bidi isolation on output. newspaper4k claims 80+ languages with optional per-language NLP extras for Chinese, Thai, Japanese, Bengali, Hindi, Nepali and Tamil -- much broader nominal coverage, but the coverage is in the stop-word lists and tokenizers, the underlying Goose scorer is still a stop-word-count heuristic with the same structural problem, and no per-language accuracy is published for any of the 80. Broad claimed coverage with no per-language evidence is a weaker position than narrow honest coverage.
leaks_outward: The sharpest split in this batch, and the reason to keep these two in one item. jusText leaks NOTHING: no network access, no telemetry, no fetcher, no model download, pure computation over text in hand. newspaper3k/4k is the OPPOSITE and is the only item in this batch that is itself a network client in its normal mode of use. It fetches the article URL; it can crawl a source's category pages; it parses RSS feeds; it downloads IMAGES in order to pick a top_image; and it runs a concurrent ThreadPoolExecutor over all of that. Each of those is a separate, session-less, differently-fingerprinted request to the origin, and the image downloads in particular are a strong crawler tell because a human reader's browser fetches images the page displays while newspaper fetches CANDIDATES to measure them. There is a further hazard worth naming explicitly: newspaper3k's nlp() path historically requires NLTK data (the punkt tokenizer) to be downloaded at first use, which is a RUNTIME NETWORK DEPENDENCY IN A MEASURED PATH -- a third-party download triggered by an extraction call. Under this project's no_mocks and reproducibility posture that is disqualifying on its own: an extraction whose behaviour depends on whether a corpus download succeeded is neither deterministic nor loud about it. [uncertain] on whether newspaper4k still triggers that download implicitly.
mechanism_detectability: jusText: zero, absolute -- never in the page, no DOM API touched, attachShadow untouched, no CDP, no extension, no timing channel, not present while the page is live. newspaper3k/4k: HIGHLY detectable server-side, and among the easiest bot signatures on the web. A default Python HTTP client User-Agent, no subresource fetching pattern resembling a browser, image requests for candidates the page never displayed, feed and category crawling in bursts, and concurrent requests from one IP are collectively an unambiguous crawler fingerprint that commodity bot management flags on sight. Client-side detectability is nil for both since neither runs in the page. The lesson for this project's architecture is a clean separation rule: an extraction ALGORITHM can be perfectly undetectable while an extraction PIPELINE that fetches is trivially detectable, and bundling the two -- which newspaper does and jusText does not -- makes the undetectable part inherit the detectable part's exposure.
countermeasures: jusText: nothing to harden, nothing offered. Its five thresholds are exposed as parameters, which is a tuning surface rather than a hardening one, though the exposure is unusually honest -- the algorithm's entire behaviour is five numbers a caller can see and change, which is the most auditable policy surface in this batch. newspaper offers Config knobs including a settable browser_user_agent, request timeout, and proxy support, which are crawler-politeness and evasion controls rather than privacy protections; setting a browser UA to blend in is impersonation, not hardening, and does not change the request pattern that gives it away. Neither has a resource guard. Against sites defending themselves, both are defeated outright by client-side rendering, and jusText is additionally defeated by any page whose content is not full sentences.
measured_fidelity_cost: Not measured against a full-capture control by anyone, for either tool. jusText's cost is at least ANALYTICALLY derivable from its thresholds, which is more than can be said for most items here: everything under 70 characters, under 30% function words, or over 0.2 link density is dropped, so the loss for a given page can be computed exactly rather than estimated -- a genuinely useful property, and one that makes jusText a good instrument for MEASURING a corpus (how much of this page is non-sentence content?) even where it is a bad instrument for reading one. newspaper publishes overlap F1 on article corpora and nothing about loss. Affordance retention is zero for both, so against this project's 80.9%-of-99.7% figure both would score 0% on the acting axis. No measurement anywhere frames loss as a hardening cost, because neither tool has a hardening dimension.
gate_state_at_capture: Not recorded by either, and jusText is actively distorted in a specific, checkable way. Consent-banner copy is medium-length, low-link-density, function-word-rich prose -- it is grammatical text about cookies -- so it clears every one of jusText's good-block criteria and is retained as content. Cookie notices are, in the algorithm's own terms, exemplary main content. Paywall teasers likewise. The one preprocessing rule that touches this space, dropping blocks containing a copyright symbol, catches footers rather than consent text. newspaper will happily return a consent wall or a paywall teaser as an article with a title, an author and a date attached, which is worse: it produces a well-formed metadata record for a page it never actually read. With roughly two-thirds of top sites presenting a consent interface, a jusText-built corpus is enriched for consent prose and a newspaper-built corpus is enriched for confidently-mislabelled gated pages, in both cases with no field to detect it afterwards.
determinism: jusText: fully deterministic within a pinned version and stoplist -- pure arithmetic over text against five fixed thresholds, no randomness, no clock, no network, no cross-call state, idempotent within a process. The stoplist is part of the input in the determinism sense and must be pinned with the version. It is, alongside Boilerpipe, the cleanest determinism story in the batch. newspaper3k/4k: NOT deterministic in normal use, and not close. Its input is a fresh network fetch, so the same call at two times returns different content; its image selection depends on which image downloads succeeded and how fast; its concurrency means multi-article runs interleave nondeterministically; and any NLTK-data-dependent path depends on filesystem state established by an earlier download. Same URL emphatically does not mean same output, and the tool provides no way to separate the fetch from the extraction if you want the latter to be reproducible -- though passing pre-fetched HTML is possible and is the only defensible way to use it.
determinism_across_versions: jusText drifts only through the HTML parser (block segmentation changes if whitespace normalisation or implied-element insertion changes) and through stoplist revisions; the five thresholds are stable published constants, which is an unusually narrow drift surface. Note the asymmetry with the benchmark row above: Trafilatura's table measures jusText with a CUSTOM configuration, so the published number tracks someone's tuning rather than the defaults, and threshold changes are a caller-side drift axis that no version pin captures. newspaper drifts through everything: extractor changes between 3k and 4k are explicitly claimed as accuracy improvements (0.9460 versus 0.2.8's lower figure), the lxml version moves underneath, the fetch layer's behaviour depends on requests/urllib3 versions and TLS stack, and the NLP extras carry their own model and data versions. Pinning newspaper reproducibly requires pinning the tool, the parser, the HTTP stack, the NLTK data and the network, of which the last is impossible.
reproducibility: jusText: high, and cheaply so -- pin (version, stoplist, parser, input bytes) and the result is exact. Its evaluation corpus (CleanEval) is a published artifact, so the historical claim is re-runnable, and Trafilatura's benchmark is re-runnable in the sense that the tool and configuration are named, though the 990-document set is not released as a public frozen artifact. newspaper: LOW, and structurally so, because the tool's default mode of use includes the fetch. A newspaper-built dataset cannot be regenerated -- the pages have changed, the images may be gone, the feeds have rotated. This is the exact failure this project already has with 75% of its corpus refetching live resources on every read, and newspaper is the cautionary version of it: a pipeline that fuses fetch and extract makes reproducibility impossible by construction, and the fix is architectural (separate capture from fold, persist the capture) rather than a matter of pinning versions.
failure_modes: jusText: (1) Total rejection of non-sentence pages -- listings, product pages, tables, code -- by design, returning empty or near-empty. (2) CONTEXT PROPAGATION ERRORS, its distinctive failure: because short and near-good blocks are resolved from the nearest unambiguous neighbours, one misclassified anchor block can flip an entire run of ambiguous blocks between two delimiters, so errors arrive in RUNS rather than singly. (3) Consent text retained as content. (4) Missing or wrong stoplist -> complete failure or garbage, depending on whether the caller noticed. (5) Heading promotion pulling a navigation heading into content when it happens to precede a good block within MAX_HEADING_DISTANCE. (6) SPA shell. newspaper: (1) Returns a confident article-shaped record for pages that are not articles. (2) Fetch failures, rate limits, and bot blocks surfacing as empty or partial articles. (3) Image downloads timing out and changing top_image between runs. (4) Author and date extraction returning attacker-controlled or simply wrong values that then look authoritative in a structured field. (5) Abandonment: newspaper3k has had no fixes since 2020, so every bug found today is permanent unless the caller migrates to 4k. (6) NLTK-data dependency failing at first call.
failure_visibility: jusText is better than average and unusually self-describing, though nobody exploits it: every block carries an explicit CLASS LABEL (good/bad/short/near-good), so the classification is inspectable per block rather than hidden inside a score, and the fraction of blocks that were resolved from context rather than classified outright is a directly available confidence proxy that no implementation surfaces. Emitting the label distribution and the ambiguous-run lengths would convert most of its silent failures into observable ones at essentially zero cost -- this is the same free-self-description opportunity Boilerpipe leaves on the table, and jusText is even better positioned because its classes are already named. Empty output is loud. newspaper is the worst failure-visibility profile in the batch: it returns a populated Article object with a title, an author, a date and a text field whether or not it read an article, so a non-article page, a paywall, a consent wall and a bot-block page all produce structurally identical, confident-looking records, and downstream code cannot distinguish them without independent checks. Silent degradation with a well-formed schema is more dangerous than silent degradation with a text blob, because the schema invites trust.
scale_limits: jusText is cheap and provably so at scale: linear in text length, a constant-time feature computation per block, a single context pass over the block sequence, and its 20 TB / 70-billion-token deployment is the strongest scale evidence in this batch after Resiliparse's DCLM use. Memory is bounded by the block sequence. newspaper's cost is dominated by NETWORK, not computation: article fetch plus image fetches plus optional feed and category crawls, parallelised across threads, so throughput is bounded by the origin's tolerance and by rate limiting rather than by CPU, and cost per article is unbounded because the image-candidate set is unbounded. The nlp() path is separately expensive and is documented as such. For any batch use, newspaper's scaling behaviour is a crawler's, with a crawler's operational and ethical footprint.
delta_cost_model: jusText has a REAL BUT WEAKER delta story than Boilerpipe, and the difference is precisely instructive. Its context-free pass is fully local: length, link density and stop-word density are computed from a block's own text, so a text edit re-classifies exactly one block. Its context-SENSITIVE pass is not local: short and near-good blocks are resolved from the nearest good/bad delimiters, so a change that flips one block's context-free class can propagate across the entire ambiguous RUN it delimits. The correct statement of the bound is therefore: recomputation is proportional to the length of the maximal ambiguous run containing the change, not to the page and not to the change. That is still sublinear in the page and still falsifiable, and stating it in exactly this form is the useful part -- it is what an honest O(delta) claim looks like when a small amount of non-locality exists, versus the silence that usually accompanies such claims. Caveats: block re-segmentation on structural mutation propagates further; heading promotion reaches forward by MAX_HEADING_DISTANCE, adding a second bounded non-local dependency; and shadow mutations, CSS-driven change, canvas and declarative shadow DOM in the initial parse are all outside the model entirely and must be accounted separately. newspaper has no delta model whatsoever -- every call is a fetch plus a full parse plus a full re-score, and the fetch alone makes any delta claim meaningless.
reanchoring_stability: jusText: no identity carried in output; blocks are ordinal, which breaks on any insertion or deletion. Its class labels are per-block and would attach naturally to an addressed node if the implementation did not flatten -- the same observation as for Boilerpipe, and the same fix (compute per addressed node, do not flatten). No content hashes, no offsets, no re-anchor rate published. newspaper: worse than none, in a specific way worth naming. It carries a document-level URL and asserts a canonical link, but its extraction returns a text blob with no internal addresses at all, and its metadata fields (author, date) are scraped from attacker-controlled markup, so the identity it does carry is both coarse and untrustworthy. Neither offers anything comparable to W3C Web Annotation dual selectors or CDC boundaries.
adversarial_exposure: jusText is the MOST exposed item in this batch on concealed content and the reasoning is not subtle: it has no visibility pass at all -- no computed style (it never has any), and unlike Readability and Resiliparse not even an inline display:none or hidden-attribute check. Its preprocessing removes <script>, <style> and <header> and nothing else. Every form of concealment therefore survives if the concealed text sits in a block that passes the thresholds. And the thresholds actively SELECT for injected instructions: an injected paragraph is by construction grammatical prose of moderate length with no links, which is a textbook good block under LENGTH_HIGH=200, STOPWORDS_HIGH=0.32 and MAX_LINK_DENSITY=0.2. Stop-word density is a prose-likeness detector, and a well-crafted prompt injection is maximally prose-like -- so the algorithm does not merely fail to filter it, it preferentially retains it while discarding the surrounding page. This is the sharpest concrete instance of the general finding that a layout-blind, prose-ranking fold is structurally exposed, and it is the reason a density-or-stopword signal must never drive inclusion. newspaper adds a distinct exposure: its metadata fields are read from page-controlled markup (meta tags, JSON-LD, byline patterns) and promoted to authoritative-looking structured fields, giving an attacker a clean high-trust channel into a schema rather than into prose.
provenance_carrying: jusText: none at any granularity -- no url, no xpath, no offsets, no capture time, no shadow depth, no gate state. Only the block class labels, which are analysis output rather than provenance. newspaper: document-level and partly forged -- it carries the source url and canonical link (genuine, caller-supplied) alongside authors, publish_date and source domain scraped from the page (attacker-controlled). That mixture is the specific hazard: a stored record where trustworthy and page-asserted provenance sit in adjacent fields with no marking to distinguish them is worse than no provenance, because downstream consumers cannot tell which fields they may rely on. If this project takes anything from newspaper's metadata record it must be the shape with a hard rule attached: fields derived from the reader's own context (url, capture time, xpath, shadow depth, gate state) and fields asserted by the page must be separately namespaced and never merged.
roundtrip_safety: Neither is a fixed point. jusText's failure is analytically clean and makes it a good demonstration: link density is a RELATIVE quantity and the context-sensitive pass depends on the presence of bad blocks as delimiters, so re-running jusText on its own output -- which has had every bad block removed -- leaves the context pass with no delimiters and the document edges (treated as bad) as its only anchors, producing a different resolution of every ambiguous block. Any extractor whose classification depends on the material it removes cannot be idempotent, and jusText states that dependency explicitly enough to prove it. newspaper's output is a text blob and a metadata record; re-running the pipeline on the blob is not defined behaviour and the fetch makes the question moot. Neither has an escaping policy -- output is raw text with newline block boundaries, so source text containing the boundary convention is indistinguishable from a boundary -- and neither claims sanitization of any kind.
token_budget_and_ordering: Neither has a budget concept, a truncation policy or an ordering contract; both emit document order. jusText contributes one thing to the ordering question that nothing else in this batch does: STOP-WORD DENSITY as a continuous, cheap, per-block score of GRAMMATICALITY, which is a different and complementary axis to Boilerpipe's text density (prose-likeness by typography). Together they distinguish 'this is dense text' from 'this is a sentence', and the pair separates a code block or a table (dense, ungrammatical) from an article paragraph (dense, grammatical) without naming either region. As an ordering peripheral that is genuinely useful, and it inherits the hard rule established under adversarial_exposure: it may inform ORDER and must never inform INCLUSION, since grammaticality is exactly the property an injected instruction maximises. It also inherits the language dependence -- a stoplist per language -- which makes it a costlier peripheral than text density and one that must fail loudly rather than silently on an unlisted language. newspaper's keyword and summary outputs are a form of prioritisation, but they are produced by a naive frequency summariser, are not tied to any budget, and add a generation step to a measured path for no fidelity gain.
representation_cost: jusText: extreme compression, typically well under 10% of source tokens on an article and 0% on non-sentence pages, which return empty. Per token saved it discards all structure beyond block boundaries and retained headings, all affordances, all state, all addressability and all provenance. Its distinguishing property is that the compression is ANALYTICALLY CHARACTERISED -- you can say exactly what was dropped (anything short, link-dense or function-word-poor) rather than describing it as 'boilerplate'. newspaper: similar compression on the text field, plus a small metadata record, plus potentially large image payloads if images are retained, so its total artifact can be larger than the page's text by a wide margin. The nlp() summary is a further lossy re-encoding whose cost is a generation call and whose loss is unquantified.
what_could_be_adopted: Three mechanisms and one anti-pattern, and the anti-pattern is as valuable as the mechanisms. (1) STOP-WORD / FUNCTION-WORD DENSITY as a per-node peripheral scalar, complementary to text density: it measures grammaticality rather than typographic density, it names no region, reads no class or id or role or geometry, and it is computable from text alone with no additional detectable access. It carries a real cost the other peripherals do not -- a stoplist per language, and honest failure on unlisted languages -- which should be surfaced as an explicit 'no stoplist, no score' rather than a silent zero. Order by it, never include by it. (2) THE FOUR-CLASS LABELLING WITH AN EXPLICIT AMBIGUOUS CLASS. jusText does not force a binary decision: 'short' and 'near-good' are first-class outcomes meaning 'I cannot tell from this node alone', and they are resolved separately and visibly. Carrying an explicit UNCERTAIN state through a fold, and reporting how much of a page landed in it, is a loud-failure mechanism available for free and used by nobody -- it is the per-node analogue of DOM Distiller's refusal gate. (3) THE FULLY-EXPOSED FIVE-PARAMETER POLICY. jusText's entire behaviour is five published numbers a caller can read, change and store with the artifact, which makes captures comparable across settings and makes the policy auditable rather than buried in a scorer. That is the same virtue as Resiliparse's toggle surface, arrived at differently. THE ANTI-PATTERN, from newspaper3k, is the most important lesson in this item: DO NOT FUSE FETCH AND FOLD. Bundling the fetcher, the crawler, the image downloader and the NLP into the extraction call is what makes newspaper undeterministic, unreproducible, trivially detectable, governance-exposed and privacy-hostile all at once, and every one of those follows from the fusion rather than from the extraction algorithm, which is unremarkable. jusText, which is the same era and the same quality of heuristic with the I/O removed, has none of those problems. Keep the capture, the fold and the actuator separable, and store what the capture saw.
constraint_violation_ledger: jusText -- structure_agnosticism: MOSTLY ADOPTABLE, with one flagged exception. Length, link density and stop-word density read no class, no id, no role, no ARIA and no URL, and block segmentation uses only the inline/block tag distinction, which is squarely 'tag plus interactivity'. The exceptions are explicit and small: discarding the contents of <header> and of <select> by tag name, and discarding blocks containing a copyright symbol, are region-and-content-pattern rules; the <header> rule in particular names a region even though it names it via a standard tag. Refuse those three rules and the remainder is compliant. The CLASSIFIER's good/bad labelling is REJECTED as region-role naming; the FEATURES are adoptable. no_layout_in_the_fold: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- no geometry anywhere, and the length thresholds are typographic proxies rather than reads. o_delta: ADOPTABLE WITH A STATED BOUND -- context-free classification is per-block local; the context-sensitive pass propagates across the maximal ambiguous run containing the change; heading promotion reaches MAX_HEADING_DISTANCE forward. Bounded and sublinear, but the bound must be stated in exactly those terms rather than claimed as O(1)-per-change. Shadow, CSS-driven, canvas and declarative-shadow-DOM changes remain outside the model. no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- pure arithmetic plus a data file, no network, no learned component, no stub surface, computable against a real live DOM. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: features ADOPTABLE AS-IS (they compute over whatever text nodes they are handed, including a composed shadow DOM's, with no need to patch attachShadow); the historical IMPLEMENTATION is NEGATIVE ORACLE ONLY, since it consumes serialized HTML, misses shadow content and emits no unreachable marker. jusText OVERALL: ADOPTABLE IN THE ACTUATOR LAYER ONLY as a component, with the stop-word-density scalar, the explicit-uncertain-class pattern and the exposed-parameter discipline adoptable as-is into the fold's design. newspaper3k/4k -- structure_agnosticism: REJECTED (Goose node scoring plus news-article priors plus byline and date pattern matching). no_layout_in_the_fold: REJECTED, and uniquely so -- it obtains image geometry BY FETCHING THE IMAGES, which is layout information acquired over the network, a violation with a privacy consequence attached. o_delta: REJECTED (fetch plus full parse plus full re-score per call). no_mocks: REJECTED -- a runtime NLTK-data download in a measured path, a network fetch whose failure changes output silently, and no way to guarantee the measured path ran against real data rather than a partially-populated cache. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: NEGATIVE ORACLE ONLY, same reasoning as above. newspaper OVERALL: REJECTED. Its value here is entirely as a worked example of what fusing fetch and fold costs.
governance_signal_handling: jusText: none, and cleanly none -- no fetcher, so no robots.txt, no Content Signals, no ai.txt, no IETF AIPREF vocabulary, no Web Bot Auth signature or Signature Agent Card, no HTTP 402 path. The obligation belongs entirely to whatever produced the HTML, which is the correct separation. newspaper: this is where the fusion bites hardest, because newspaper IS a crawler -- it walks category pages, parses feeds and fetches image candidates -- and I could not confirm that it consults robots.txt at all [uncertain]; the documentation does not address it, and the original newspaper3k was widely criticised on exactly this point. A crawler that does not read robots.txt, presents a library User-Agent, offers a settable browser User-Agent as a Config option, and fetches images the page never displayed is on the wrong side of every emerging access-determining signal -- Content Signals, AIPREF, Web Bot Auth, HTTP 402 -- none of which it implements. For this project the takeaway is defensive: adopting anything from newspaper must not drag its fetch layer along, because the fetch layer is where the governance exposure lives, and this project's favourable position (reading a page the user's own browser already loaded in the user's own session) is destroyed the moment the tool makes a request of its own.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: jusText retains nothing and hands the caller prose stripped of metadata: no url, no capture time, no gate state, no author. That is minimal by accident rather than by design, and it cuts both ways -- less identifying metadata stored, but also no basis on which to run a legitimate-interest balancing test, and no way to distinguish editorial copy from user-generated content, since forum posts and comments that clear 70 characters and 30% function words are retained as content with no marker and no toggle. Consent-text enrichment compounds this. newspaper is materially worse under EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 because it retains MORE personal data by design and stores it in named fields: AUTHORS is a first-class extracted field (personal data, structured, queryable), publish_date is retained, images are downloaded and may be stored (images of people, fetched and persisted, are a distinct and higher-risk category than text), and the crawler mode accumulates many pages per source in one operation, which shifts the activity from incidental reading toward systematic collection -- the framing most likely to attract regulatory attention. The stored artifact is the regulated act for both, but newspaper's artifact is a structured personal-data record with binary attachments while jusText's is a text blob, and the difference matters for a data-minimisation argument. [uncertain] on the precise EDPB 03/2026 treatment of scraped byline metadata as a distinct category from body text.
